title: Listy
description: A high-performance list that supports grouping and can virtualize long data sets.
whenToUse:
- When you need to render a long list without paying the cost of mounting every row — enable `virtual` to render only the rows in view.
- When the list needs grouped sections with sticky headers.
- When you need imperative control over scroll position (jump to an item, a group, or a pixel offset).

examples.name: Basic
Virtual scrolling
examples.description: A long list of 10,000 rows. Set `virtual` and `height` to enable virtual scrolling, so only the rows in view are rendered.

examples.name: Grouping and sticky headers
examples.description: Use `group` to derive a group key from each item and render group headers. With `sticky` enabled, the current group header sticks to the top while scrolling.

examples.name: Rich content
examples.description: `itemRender` can render arbitrarily rich content, and rows do not need the same height.

examples.name: Drag sorting
examples.description: Implement drag sorting for list items by integrating the third-party library dnd-kit.

examples.name: Infinite loading
examples.description: Detect in `onScroll` that the list is about to reach the bottom, then load the next page on demand for endless scrolling. Combined with `virtual`, only the rows in view are rendered no matter how much data piles up.

examples.name: Custom semantic dom styling
examples.description: Customize the semantic DOM styles of Listy with `classNames` and `styles`.
